en: The Scripture on the Method for Prohibiting the Hundred Transformations of Vajra Ucchuṣma, in one fascicle.
Translated by the Tripiṭaka Master from North India,
the Śramaṇa Ajitasena (whose name means "Invincible" in the language of Tang).
At that time, Vajrapāṇi again addressed the Buddha, saying:
"World-Honored One, if there should be any son or daughter of good family who upholds this mantra of mine and yet experiences no efficacy, such a thing is impossible."
If one wishes to cause a mountain to collapse,
one should take three *śrōṇa* of white mustard seeds and high-quality *agaru* incense;
this should be done at a mountain where it is suspected that treasure is hidden.
Take one blade of tempered steel,
draw lines to demarcate a four-sided boundary,
and prepare one clean cloth for the ears and one incense burner.
Burn agalloch incense while first reciting the mantra one thousand and eight times.
Take white mustard seeds and scatter them in all directions until the seventh recitation.
By performing this rite, the mountain will collapse of its own accord.
If there is a place where treasures are hidden, the deity of that treasury will relinquish the treasures and depart, allowing them to be used as one pleases.
If one wishes to cause the ocean to dry up,
one should first recite the mantra one thousand and eight times.
Fashion a dragon in the shape of a serpent out of gold or copper and cast it into the ocean; immediately the sea shall dry up.
If one wishes to cause rivers and streams to flow upstream, [one should do so].
Take guggulu incense and fashion it into the shape of an elephant.
Regardless of its size, cast it into the water and recite the mantra one hundred and eight times;
immediately, the current will flow backward.
To restore it to its former state, one should recite the mantra over a clean stone and cast it into the water; the water will then become as it was before.
Should there be thunder, lightning, thunderbolts, venomous dragons, sudden winds, or violent rains, [this shall likewise prevail].
Then, perform the mudrā for stopping lightning and thunder:
with the left hand, bend the middle, ring, and little fingers together into the palm;
the index finger and thumb [are held as follows].
Press the middle joint of the index finger,
recite the mantra to empower it,
and point the seal from afar toward the location of the thunder and hail; they will cease of their own accord.
If one wishes to cause all ghosts and spirits to come of their own accord to submit and serve as messengers,
take three pecks of water and place them in a copper vessel,
surrounding it with pure ashes.
Then, one forms the Seal of Gathering and Recording:
join the two ring fingers together, bending them into the palms so that their backs rest against each other.
The tips of the two middle fingers are pressed together;
the two index fingers and the two little fingers are each shaped like opening flowers,
with the thumbs pressing against their middle joints.
Recite the mantra silently one hundred and eight times.
Then all the malevolent spirits within that world will gather like clouds and manifest their own forms.
Abandoning their poisonous and evil intentions, they shall submit to the practitioner's commands.
If one is confined by a mountain, one should recite the mantra one hundred times and shout three loud cries at the mountain where one has arrived.
Then, perform the Karma-parvata-mudrā: with the right hand,
bend the ring finger into the palm,
and extend the middle, index, and thumb fingers straight upward.
Then, holding the hands straight up with the palms facing upward, perform this mudrā seven times;
immediately thereafter, retreat seven paces.
Next is the Seven-Seal Mountain.
Within that mountain, all birds and beasts have been moved out.
If one performs this seal-mantra seven times, [the result follows].
Seal it toward the sky twenty-one times;
not even a speck of dust will pass through the air.
If one wishes to cause a person to remain silent:
Write down the person's name and place it inside their mouth;
that person will then be unable to speak.
Upon uttering it, one attains speech.
If reciting any other mantras, one must first construct an altar;
however, if reciting this mantra of mine, there is no need to construct an altar.
One should merely fashion a single vajra-goad (vajrāṅkuśa) from *vaji* wood;
then, within a Buddhist stūpa or a quiet chamber,
smear the ground with fragrant clay according to its dimensions.
Adorn it with various incenses and flowers as an offering.
Place the ritual mallet within the mandala and recite the mantra one hundred and eight times;
the mallet will then move of its own accord.
Even if it transforms into various different objects, do not find this strange.
Recite the mantra once more one hundred and eight times,
and the mallet will naturally rise three feet above the ground.
Whether it be five, six, seven, or even ten feet in height,
the practitioner of the Dharma must immediately take refuge, repent, and make vows;
I shall then manifest my true body within that [image].
Whatever the practitioner’s heart desires and finds joy in,
all shall be swiftly attained according to their wishes;
I shall immediately bestow upon them the prediction of enlightenment (bodhy-avyākaraṇa).
One will immediately attain liberation of body and mind.
First, one must complete one hundred thousand recitations;
only then may the ritual be performed. If the required count has not been fulfilled, no efficacious results will be obtained.
The second seal of the mudrā-dharma: carve this seal to a size of one inch and eight fen.
Recite the mantra one thousand times daily and seal it with white resin incense.
Carve the seal on a day when it is not seen by others.
Use the seal to seal the heart;
thereby one attains the wisdom of the heart, natural wisdom, and the wisdom of past lives.
Maintain the mudrā for one hundred days;
you will immediately attain various great Dharma gates.
[The] seal is one inch and two fen square; recite the mantra six hundred times.
Consecrate it with agalloch incense.
Wearing it while traveling will cause all people to love and delight in one, attain great mastery, and be forever freed from all sufferings.
Carve the seal to measure one and five-tenths inches square.
Recite the mantra six hundred times.
Consecrate it with white resin incense (śrīkhaṇḍa) and seal the feet with the mudrā.
One will then be able to fly through the void, moving with sovereign mastery wherever one desires.
Carve the seal to a size of one inch and eight fen,
and seal it with white resinous incense (*śrīkhaṇḍa*).
Recite the mantra seven thousand times and seal one's feet with the mudrā;
one may then travel three million li in a single day without anyone being able to see them.
The Divine Transformation Method Seal for Extending Life.
Write this upon the heart and the ailment will immediately be cured.
Greatly auspicious! Swiftly and urgently, as per the sacred command!
Seal the heart and ache;
by writing this, the ailment is immediately eliminated.
Great good fortune! Swiftly, as per the command! First recite the mantra seven times.
For those afflicted by demonic illnesses or possessed by spirits and malevolent ghosts, write [the mantra] in vermilion and swallow it.
Zhu Tongzhi’s seven large-character inscriptions stood upright and were proven effective in curing illnesses with divine efficacy.
If one follows the ritual instructions,
they take two zhang, one chi, and seven cun of white sandalwood silk.
Wrap it in white silk and place it within the world-system of the Earth-Wheel (Dharaṇī-cakra).
This will cause people to extend their lifespan, reaching seventy years of age.
If there is no one to escort it,
one may place it in the middle of the courtyard of one's own home;
it is also permissible to bury it by digging seven feet into the ground.
Furthermore, one will attain intelligence, great wisdom, and unimpeded eloquence.
These seven medicinal paths can also cure ten thousand ailments;
swallowing them brings about longevity and increases wisdom, possessing great and proven efficacy.
The seven paths above are to be written in vermilion upon paper;
swallowing a thousand such tablets will cause one to prolong life,
attaining a lifespan equal to that of Heaven and Earth.
One must not allow others to see it. If there are those who suffer from any illness,
by writing this talisman for them, all shall be cured.
If a person writes these talismans and swallows them,
it will be a great and proven efficacy for extending one's years and increasing one's wisdom.
Regarding these seven methods above, if there are those who seek various kinds of rare treasures:
Write this talisman in vermilion and swallow it;
after seven full days, various kinds of wonderful jewels will arrive spontaneously.
If one seeks the wealth and property of others, [the same shall occur].
One should write the person's name beneath the talisman;
that person will immediately deliver the goods.
These three aforementioned talismans should be written in vermilion ink upon the four legs of the bed.
The eight great *vajrapāṇi* constantly provide protection, never for a moment abandoning him.
You must strictly maintain purity and ensure that no defiled objects enter the room;
you must exercise the utmost caution.
If a great fire disaster breaks out,
write a talisman and cast one into the fire while reciting the mantra one hundred and eight times;
in an instant, the disaster will extinguish itself.
If a malignant fire or wind arises,
write this talisman and mantra one hundred and eight times and cast it into the wind; it will immediately cease.
If a great flood arises,
write this talisman and cast it into the water;
immediately the flowing current will cease, and people will not be drowned.
When there is heavy rain,
write this dhāraṇī-mantra one hundred and eight times and cast it toward the rain;
the rain will immediately subside of its own accord.
Write this talisman in vermilion ink and swallow three pieces;
you may also write it for others, and it will immediately produce efficacious results.
If it were not so, the use of these various talismans would be ineffective.
At that time, after Vajra Kṣitigarbha (Vaiśramaṇa) had spoken these talismans,
the great assembly praised him with one voice, saying:
"Excellent, Great Malla! You are able to speak this great and wondrous Dharma, causing all sentient beings to attain liberation.
At that time, Vajra-kṣaṇa addressed the great assembly:
You should know that wherever this Dharma of mine circulates among you, we,
the Great Devas, shall always protect those who practice this Dharma and assist them in achieving success.
At that time, Vajra spoke again, saying:
"If there are sentient beings who practice this dharma,
I shall immediately go to them and manifest before those individuals."
I shall also grant whatever aspirations they seek,
enabling them to achieve various manifestations and various supernormal powers without obstruction;
they must always mindfully recollect my original teacher, Śākyamuni Buddha.
I shall then constantly follow them,
causing all dharmas to assist in their accomplishment.
At that time, Vajra, having spoken this dharma, [remained silent].
The great assembly was all the more filled with both sorrow and joy;
likewise, the devas, nāgas, and great spirits each received the holy words, prostrated at his feet, and departed.
*The Scripture of the Vajra of Foul Traces Prohibiting a Hundred Transformations*, one fascicle; the ancient manuscript contains forty-three characters of dharani.
During the reign of Emperor Taizong of the Tang dynasty, many people maintained its recitation, and their spiritual responses were manifold.
Removing the cross-shaped symbols, I now transcribe this for you.
There is no mantra superior to this for swiftly obtaining spiritual efficacy.

Oṃ hrīḥ hūṃ mahāparakrama ṭi kvaṃ kvaṃ (he) (ma) (ni) ṇa ki ṇa manaśe (oṃ) (c) (k) (j) (na) u śemu hūṃ hūṃ (hūṃ) phaṭ phaṭ phaṭ (phaṭ) (phaṭ) svāhā. This is the divine mantra transmitted by the Master of True Awakening.
It is the same as the mantra in this present sutra;

however, due to the phonetic transcriptions of the Sanskrit sounds, there are slight differences in the characters and words. Oṃ buddha kūṭa jyotir mahā-prajñā-hana khur muṃ phaṭ muṃ vike vi manasi uṣṇīṣa kūṭa hūṃ hūṃ hūṃ phaṭ phaṭ phaṭ svāhā.
